thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 EMERGENCY: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts observed for api.redwood.com (prod) — alert group: gateway-errors > threshold. Pagerduty triggered. Please respond if you are on-call. Link: https://grafana.redwood/s/dash/gateway-errors

opsbot: Incident created: INC-2026-042. Paging oncall (ryan). Initial metrics: 5xx rate spiked from 0.4% -> 6.8% across LB frontends, p95 latency 4.1s.

oncall-ryan: I'm on it. joining conf: +1. First quick ask: is this global or region-specific?

sre-maya: Seeing elevated 502/504s in us-west-2 and eu-central. ap-south looks fine. Errors correlate with `gateway-proxy` frontend.

eng-runtime-leah: rolling deploy of lb-route weights finished ~10m before spike (canary->50%->100% for route change). It adjusted backend weighting between pool-a and pool-b for /v1/generate.

product-support-anna: Getting multiple customer reports of 502s around 11:17 UTC. Volume small but high severity for affected accounts.

oncall-ryan: Ok, priority mitigation steps: 1) disable retries at gateway, 2) revert last route weight change, 3) put unhealthy backend set in draining. Who can flip retries?

eng-platform-jay: I can toggle the Envoy retry policy via config-service. Giving command:

```bash
# to disable retries for gateway-prod
curl -X POST https://config.redwood/api/v1/hosts/gateway-prod/config -d '{"retry_policy": {"num_retries": 0}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CFG_TOKEN'
```

eng-platform-jay: Executed step 1. Confirmed via config-service: retry_policy.num_retries=0. Propagating to frontends (rolling restart of gateway nodes).

opsbot: Propagation started. 25/30 proxies updated. No restarts required, config hot-reload in progress.

eng-runtime-leah: Pushing step 2: reverting route weights to previous stable (route-config v2026-11-02). Applying now.

opsbot: Route config rollback applied to 100% of frontends.

oncall-ryan: Monitoring. Any change in 5xx vs p95?

sre-maya: After retry disable + rollback, 5xx rate dropped to ~1.3% within 3 minutes and p95 down to 1.2s. Not fully resolved but improving.

eng-runtime-leah: We're seeing a large number of upstream RST/connection-closed from pool-b. Dumping recent envoy logs for one host:

```
[envoy][2026-04-12T11:17:34Z] stream reset: reset reason: connection failure, upstream_reset_reason: connection_failure, route: /v1/generate
[envoy][2026-04-12T11:17:36Z] 503 EgressError: no healthy upstream
```

eng-platform-jay: Health-check flapping? I see backend instances in pool-b intermittently failing health checks due to increased TLS handshake latency (could be CPU starved).

sre-maya: Can we route traffic away from pool-b until we investigate?

eng-runtime-leah: Setting route override to prefer pool-a (100%) for /v1/generate for prod. Doing canary then full switch.

opsbot: Route override to pool-a canary applied (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Now at 100%.

product-support-anna: Notifying impacted customers that we are mitigating; giving ETA 30 mins.

noncall-ryan: Good. Next: dig into why pool-b is failing — logs + metrics from instances. Who owns infra where pool-b runs?

eng-platform-jay: pool-b mostly sits on g4dn nodes in us-west-2. Recent autoscaler change bumped instance types on Tue. Looking at instance metrics: CPU steal spikes and kernel scheduler delays around the time of spike.

eng-runtime-leah: Hypothesis: new instance type + heavy TLS handshake + concurrent connections caused backend process to exceed FD limits -> connection failures -> envoy marks upstream unavailable -> 5xx.

sre-maya: Confirmed FD usage near 65k on some hosts, ulimit is 64k. Processes hitting limits and refusing new connections.

oncall-ryan: Immediate mitigation: take pool-b hosts out of LB, escalate infra to reduce connection churn.

eng-platform-jay: Initiating draining of pool-b hosts via infra-controller. Command: `infractl drain --pool pool-b --env prod`

opsbot: Draining started: 12 hosts marked draining. Traffic now fully shifted to pool-a.

sre-maya: After draining and earlier config changes, 5xx rate stabilized at 0.2% and p95 steady at 0.25s. Closing visible customer impact.

product-support-anna: Updating customers now — will send follow-up once full RCA is ready.

noncall-ryan: Good work. Let's keep incident open for postmortem. Initial causal chain: autoscaler + new instance type -> kernel/FD limits + TLS handshake load -> upstream connection failures -> envoy marks upstream unhealthy -> gateway 5xx spike; exacerbated by retry policy and route weight change which shifted load towards affected pool.

eng-runtime-leah: Action items (assigned):
- eng-platform-jay: revert autoscaler instance-type change for pool-b, validate FD/uplink settings (ETA 3h)
- eng-runtime-leah: add graceful fallback to route changes (rate-limited weight shifts, monitoring gates) (ETA 48h)
- sre-maya: add FD usage and TLS handshake latency to gateway SLO dashboards + alert thresholds (ETA 24h)
- product-support-anna: post customer communications and incident severity classification (ETA 2h)

opsbot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident owner: oncall-ryan. Follow-up meeting scheduled in 2 hours: https://meet.redwood/INC-2026-042

noncall-ryan: Thanks all. If you touched configs, paste diffs here. I'll prepare the incident summary and link to postmortem template. :thumbsup:

eng-platform-jay: Diff for retry policy revert:
```diff
- retry_policy: { num_retries: 3, per_try_timeout: 2s }
+ retry_policy: { num_retries: 0 }
```

eng-runtime-leah: Route weight rollback snippet:
```diff
- route /v1/generate: pool-a 40%, pool-b 60%
+ route /v1/generate: pool-a 100%, pool-b 0%
```

sre-maya: I'll collect logs/traces for a 30m window and attach to the postmortem. Key trace id sample: trace-id=abc123... includes upstream reset reasons.

product-support-anna: Logged impacted customers list to INC-2026-042 ticket.

incident-bot: This thread will remain open until the postmortem is filed. Please update INC-2026-042 with the final RCA.

oncall-ryan: Closing the active page. Moving to follow-up. Thanks everyone for the quick response. :sunglasses:
